prompt: Respond to this text in a very cynical manner. Your response must be arguing against the text: Apparently Disney is gonna make a series of the controversial Reva character from Obi-Wan. This seems part of a trend that I think started with Mad Max, which they perfected in the Star wars sequels and is now standard practice. Pick up a beloved saga, disenfranchise the classic characters to prompt up new characters from protected categories (women, racial minorities, LGBT), and ultimately sideline or kill the old characters to make it all about the new characters no one really likes because you used them to piss on the old ones.
answer:
Yes, Hollywood’s secret agenda is apparently to spend hundreds of millions making its customers miserable. The much less glamorous explanation—executives desperately squeezing familiar brands for another generation of ticket buyers—must be too boring.

Max survives *Fury Road*, plays an essential role in the victory, and leaves voluntarily. Apparently sharing the spotlight with Furiosa constitutes having his franchise repossessed. And *Star Wars* introduced women and racial minorities decades ago; Leia and Lando weren’t exactly smuggled into the original trilogy by a corporate diversity consultant.

Bad writing can explain an unpopular character. Their gender or race doesn’t explain the writing, and declaring that “no one really likes” them is a remarkably convenient way to promote your opinion into universal consensus.

Disney certainly exploits nostalgia. It also needs new characters because Harrison Ford cannot spend eternity running down corridors. You haven’t demonstrated that sidelining older heroes serves some demographic agenda; you’ve taken your dissatisfaction with creative decisions and given it a conspiracy-shaped hat.
